now: All eight refactor phases are in (DECISIONS #61-#70): a hunt is a closed loop walked past fixed spawn slots, proximity starts a real turn-based fight, a defeated wild is thrown at against a per-species pity floor, money is earned only by selling, evolution is a paid-for button, and the trainer has a level that gates the map.

baseline.note: demo city at noon. Real numbers, but the scene has no buildings, no NPCs and no characters yet.

open.what: The lead is not chosen for the matchup: a Water starter walks into a Grass wood, and the faint-swap takes the next party member in line rather than the right one. The move-priority list makes this addressable by a player; the automation still does not do it. (DECISIONS #70(j))
`pacing.js MEASURED` projects an income model that DECISIONS #69 deleted. The table is stale and the header (`pacing.js:22`) says so. (DECISIONS #70(j))
`biome.walk` -- the pre-loop scripted routes -- is still read by `index.js:363` and by `showcase.js:66`. Two ways to move a party through a biome, one of them superseded.
Slots thin as the circuit bends: 9 at four corners, 5 at twenty, because a bent ring has fewer cells at Chebyshev 2 that are not already path.
The coast circuit runs through inland grass rather than along the shoreline -- the bend heuristic prefers path/tallgrass, and the shore is neither.
`go()` is serialised but not cancellable: once a scene starts building, the player waits for it.
Travelling mid-encounter calls `encounter.cancel()` with no prompt. A silent loss of a fight the player was in.
Accuracy and evasion stages are not modelled -- deliberate, and stated at `stats.js:41`. Only the five battle stats stage.

Daylight frames have no motivated light source, which is what four rounds of blind A/B judging lost on every time. Night and cave frames, which have practicals, win. See `docs/STATUS-ARCHIVE.json` -> gate.blindJudging.
